title: Broccoli and cauliflower, cooked, no added fat

content.title: About
content.content: Broccoli and cauliflower are two cruciferous vegetables rich in vitamins, minerals, and dietary fiber. When steamed or boiled without added fat they retain most of their nutrients and have a mild, tender flavor.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Broccoli is often called a “super‑vegetable” because of its high glucoraphanin content, a compound with potential anti‑cancer effects.
Cauliflower gets its name from the resemblance of its curd to a flower head.
Both vegetables are excellent sources of vitamin C: 100 g of broccoli provides over 90 % of the daily value, cauliflower about 70 %.
Their fiber content supports a healthy gut microbiome.
Cooking without fat keeps the calorie count low—about 30 kcal per 100 g.

items.title: Immune support
items.content: Vitamin C and antioxidants help strengthen the immune system and combat free radicals.

items.title: Bone health
items.content: Calcium, vitamin K, and magnesium contribute to strong bones.

items.title: Reduced risk of chronic disease
items.content: Phytochemicals such as sulforaphane may lower inflammation and decrease the risk of heart disease.

items.title: Digestive health
items.content: Dietary fiber promotes regular bowel movements and a healthy gut.

items.title: Weight management
items.content: Low calories and high satiety help control appetite.

items.title: Gas and bloating
items.content: Cruciferous vegetables can cause gas in people with sensitive digestion.

items.title: Thyroid interaction
items.content: Large amounts of raw broccoli may affect iodine absorption, but the risk is minimal when cooked.

items.title: Allergy
items.content: Rarely, individuals may be allergic to broccoli or cauliflower.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve as a side dish, add to salads, soups, or casseroles. Steam for 5‑7 minutes to keep a slight crunch and preserve nutrients. Season with lemon juice, herbs, or a pinch of salt if desired.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep in the refrigerator in an airtight container for up to 5 days. For longer storage, blanch 2‑3 minutes and freeze in portion‑size bags.
